rows.feature: The schedule's place on the project page
rows.what: The project's Management tab opens on its Milestones sub-tab (beside Tasks, Materials, Floor Plan): the Gantt at a desk, a card list below 1024px; old ?tab=timeline links land there.
rows.v2: Project › Schedule (its own tab, third of seven, /projects/{id}/schedule)
rows.how: Its own tab instead of a sub-tab of Management; one component serves the desk and the phone.

rows.feature: Upcoming milestones on the project's Overview
rows.what: An Overview card lists the next two open milestones with “due in 3d” / “108d overdue”, with View timeline, or “No timeline set up yet” and Set timeline.
rows.v2: Project › Overview › Coming up (this week and next) and Progress (n of m milestones, with its bar), each opening the Schedule
rows.how: Coming up lists what starts or ends this week and next (else the next three dates); Progress counts milestones done; day counts are calendar days in words, never “w”.

rows.feature: A notice opens the milestone it is about
rows.what: A homeowner's approval or revision notice links to ?tab=management&milestone={id}, but the page ignores the milestone part, so nothing opens.
rows.v2: Every schedule bell row, Needs you row and Activity line opens the Schedule with that milestone's panel open (?open={id})
rows.how: It works: the address opens the milestone's panel.

rows.feature: Empty state with five ways to start a timeline
rows.what: With no milestones the pane shows “Set up your project timeline” with five choices: work phases + payments (Recommended), work phases from the quote, payment schedule only, a property-type template, or from scratch.
rows.v2: Project › Schedule › Set up the schedule: Works start on, then A quote · A schedule template · An uploaded quote · Drafted by Maison AI · Nothing yet, with What you will get drawn before anything is made
rows.how: One card with the works start day and a source picker that previews the result; the payment-only and hybrid ways are gone (payments are diamonds on work milestones); the first pick follows Settings › Projects.

rows.feature: Start from the project's quote (work phases)
rows.what: Picks this project's quote, or the lead's as a fallback, and makes one milestone per work category, laid end to end.
rows.v1: Empty state › Work phases from quote › Generate from a quote
rows.v2: Set up the schedule (or Rebuild) › A quote — any of the lead's quotes, the signed one first
rows.how: Rules, not AI: the quote's trades become site stages in the order work runs (its sections when no line names a trade), at usual lengths with the usual overlaps.

rows.feature: AI-written plan from the quote, with tips and risk warnings
rows.what: POST /api/projects/plan asks Gemini for phases with lengths and colours; tips and risk warnings are saved but never shown; when the AI fails a mechanical plan arrives under the same success toast.
rows.v1: Empty state / cog › From work categories
rows.v2: Set up the schedule / Rebuild › Drafted by Maison AI; Schedule ⋮ › Draft with Maison AI…
rows.how: A curated rule-based draft labelled Maison AI — no model call and no AI credits; it shows what it read, why each milestone is there and 1.0's tips and risks (Worth knowing) for review before it lands. A real model is for developers to wire.

rows.feature: Hybrid: work phases plus payment markers
rows.what: Builds the work phases and adds each payment stage as its own one-day amber milestone, spread from the first day to handover.
rows.v1: Empty state / cog › Hybrid — work + payments
rows.v2: Setting up any schedule ties the payment stages to work milestones (a diamond on the bar)
rows.how: No separate payment milestones: the first stage after signing falls due as works start, the last at the handover, the others on the milestone ending nearest their estimate.

rows.feature: A timeline of payment milestones only
rows.what: One amber bar per payment stage (Deposit / Progress / Final; studio default 10/30/30/30), tiled across the span, no AI call.
rows.v1: Empty state / cog › Payment schedule only
rows.how: A payment is a stage tied to a work milestone, not a milestone of its own.

rows.feature: Upload a quote file to generate the timeline
rows.what: Accepts PDF, image, CSV or Excel, parses it on the server (/api/quotes/parse), saves the lines onto the project as its quote and generates work phases (ignoring a Hybrid pick).
rows.v1: Generate from a quote › Upload a new quote; cog › Upload quote to enable
rows.v2: Set up the schedule / Rebuild › An uploaded quote
rows.how: Read in the browser by Upload a quote's reader: spreadsheets for real; a PDF or a photo only when it is one of the demo's reference quotes — real document reading is for developers. The file is not kept as the project's quote.

rows.feature: Ready-made timelines per property type
rows.what: Five templates for the region (HDB BTO, HDB Resale, Condo, Landed, Commercial Fit-out in Singapore; Malaysia, UAE and India have their own), the closest preselected; milestones laid end to end from today.
rows.v1: Empty state › Start from a template › Pick a template
rows.v2: Company › Templates › Schedules › the five ready-made schedules; Set up the schedule preselects the one for the property type
rows.how: Singapore's five only — 1.0's Malaysia, UAE and India sets are not carried (regions beyond Singapore are not built). They lay out from works start, not today, and a studio may edit or delete them.

rows.feature: Start from scratch
rows.what: Opens the New milestone dialog to add milestones one at a time (on desktop the dialog is not mounted while the timeline is empty, so the press seems to do nothing).
rows.v2: Set up the schedule › Nothing yet (opens Add milestone on the works start day)

rows.feature: Starting a timeline on a phone
rows.what: Below 1024px the empty state offers only Add milestone — no quote, schedule or template.
rows.v2: The same Set up the schedule card on a phone (the picker as one select, the preview folded)
rows.how: A phone can start from a quote, a template, an upload or Maison AI's draft too.

rows.feature: A timeline as a set-up gate (Draft → Active)
rows.what: “Project timeline created” is one of five checks before a Draft project goes Active; the card has no link to it and Complete setup has no step for it.
rows.v2: Getting started › Schedule (Set up); Start the project sheet › The schedule; Overview › Needs you
rows.how: A set-up item, not a gate: the Start sheet offers the schedule in the same press, and Needs you keeps asking until there is one.

rows.feature: Regenerate or reset a timeline that exists
rows.what: The cog's Generate timeline (four generators) and Reset to a template replace every milestone and its id behind a browser confirm, losing statuses, links, publish state, task and invoice ties.
rows.v1: Gantt toolbar › cog › Generate timeline · From project template
rows.v2: Schedule ⋮ › Rebuild the schedule… (a quote, a template or an uploaded quote)
rows.how: Keeps every milestone the new list names — its id, dates, status, tasks, payment and the client's answers — adds the new ones, takes off the rest after a confirm naming them, and offers Undo.

rows.feature: Set up a schedule mid-job
rows.what: Every generated or templated milestone starts Not started, whatever the date (a rule after an earlier seed left projects with several running bars).
rows.v2: Set up the schedule marks milestones that ended before today Done and today's In progress, and says so
rows.how: A schedule made mid-job knows what already happened.

rows.feature: Save a timeline as a template
rows.what: Saves the milestones (name, day offsets, description, colour, payment %, commission flag, links by position) with a name and description.
rows.v1: Gantt toolbar › cog › Save as template
rows.v2: Schedule ⋮ › Save as a template (to Company › Templates › Schedules)
rows.how: Asks a name only; each item keeps its name, length, gap after the one before and whether the client confirms it — not a description, a colour, several links or a payment % (payments come from the quote).

rows.feature: Manage saved timeline templates
rows.what: A settings page lists saved templates with rename and delete; built-in ones cannot be changed.
rows.v2: Company › Templates › Schedules (Schedule ⋮ › Manage schedule templates)
rows.how: One library with folders: new, edit in its own editor, rename, duplicate, delete with restore; the ready-made ones are ordinary rows; four 1.0 template stores became this one.

rows.feature: Reset to a template (saved and built-in per project type)
rows.what: Lists the studio's saved templates and six built-in “{type} — Standard” templates with payment splits; applying one anchors it on the first milestone's start and resets every status.
rows.v1: Gantt toolbar › cog › From project template
rows.v2: Set up the schedule / Rebuild › A schedule template
rows.how: One library; the built-ins are the five ready-made schedules and “Start from a whole-home renovation”, with no payment splits.

rows.feature: One default timeline per project type
rows.what: For each project type a list of milestones (name, days, colour) with reorder and Reset to default; its lists fed no live path into the Gantt.
rows.v2: Settings › Projects › Schedule › Where a schedule starts, by project type (Studio default, then each type)
rows.how: Each project type picks a template from the one library, the signed quote, or the property type's ready-made schedule — instead of keeping its own list.

rows.feature: Project types with milestone and payout templates
rows.what: Studio project types (category, typical duration) each with milestone templates: offset, duration, payment %, payment criteria, notes to the homeowner and a designer payout rule; nothing else reads them.
rows.how: Project type stays the Won step's three; timelines live in Company › Templates › Schedules, splits in Payment schedules, commission in Settings › Finance.

rows.feature: KPI strip (Completed, On Track %, At Risk, Duration)
rows.what: Four tiles: milestones completed of all, the share not at risk, the at-risk count and the chart's span in weeks (never under twelve).
rows.v2: Schedule › Where the job stands: one sentence, its line, and Done n of m · To handover n days · Next payment
rows.how: No On Track % or At Risk count; the headline says what is late, what moved or what runs now; the figures are real days to handover and the next payment.

rows.feature: Internal view / Client-facing view and the homeowner preview
rows.what: A toggle swaps the chart for what the homeowner sees (the portal's timeline from the published copies), with Open as homeowner (a 30-minute read-only portal) and a Preview homeowner view dialog in the cog.
rows.v1: Gantt › Internal View | Client-Facing View; cog › Preview homeowner view
rows.v2: Schedule toolbar line (“{client} sees the schedule shared on …”) opens the What {client} sees pane; Invite to Portal panel › See it as {client}
rows.how: The pane sits beside the list (a drawer below 1200px) and draws the last shared copy with the live answers; the whole portal opens read-only from the access panel.

rows.feature: Publish N changes button
rows.what: A button above the chart, shown while anything is unpublished, opens the first-publish wizard or the batch dialog; disabled when locked or payments are not 100%.
rows.v2: Schedule toolbar › Share N changes (Share the schedule the first time; Ask to share… under approval)

rows.feature: Payments must total 100% banner
rows.what: A yellow or red banner when the milestones' payment % does not add to 100, which blocks every publish button.
rows.how: Milestones carry no %; the shares come from the quote's payment schedule.

rows.feature: Contract changed by a variation order — Rebalance
rows.what: When approved VOs move the contract, a banner offers Rebalance (the publish wizard's totals step).
rows.v2: Project › Money (variation orders; invoices re-sized by the rebalance)
rows.how: Rebalancing is Money's job and the agreed shares never move; the schedule shows no banner.

rows.feature: Dependency-violation banner and “Why?”
rows.what: A red banner names milestones that start before what they depend on ends; Why? asks mAIson for options.
rows.v2: Schedule timeline: a link line turns red and dashed when a milestone starts before its link allows
rows.how: No banner or AI question: a move carries what follows, so a drag cannot break a link; only a typed date can, and the line shows it.

rows.feature: “This timeline isn't visible to your homeowner yet”
rows.what: Until the first publish a banner offers Configure & publish (the wizard).
rows.v2: Schedule toolbar line “{client} hasn't seen the schedule yet” + Share the schedule; Overview › Needs you
rows.how: The button shares directly, saying truthfully whether the client can open their portal yet.

rows.feature: Add a milestone
rows.what: Add Milestone, the list's + and Start from scratch open “New milestone”: name, short description, start and end, position, colour, depends on, payment trigger % and commission.
rows.v2: Schedule toolbar › Add milestone; row ⋮ › Add a milestone after; on a phone, Add milestone at the foot
rows.how: Asks the name only; it lands after the last one (or the one whose ⋮ was used), follows it and starts the next weekday; dates, links, colour and the rest are set in its panel. No payment % or commission switch.

rows.feature: Full screen
rows.what: A toolbar button puts the whole pane over the page; Escape leaves.
rows.v2: Schedule toolbar › Full screen (Esc or the same button leaves)

rows.feature: Autosave of the whole timeline
rows.what: The Gantt keeps a local copy and saves the whole array 1.5 s after any change (Saving… / Saved); the drawer's Cancel cannot undo what is already in it.
rows.v2: Every change saves on the server at once and answers in one sentence with Undo; the panel's Save and Cancel mean what they say
rows.how: One milestone per write, nothing lost to a race.

rows.feature: The Gantt: names beside bars, scrolling sideways
rows.what: A hand-built chart: a name list on the left, a week grid scrolling sideways with one bar per milestone, a Today marker and dependency arrows.
rows.v2: Schedule › the list that is also the timeline (frozen name column and actions, the house sideways bar)
rows.how: One table: the name column stays put, screen readers read rows and cells, and J / K walk the milestones.

rows.feature: Resize the name column
rows.what: Drag the handle between names and grid, 180–400px, not remembered.
rows.v2: Schedule › Milestone head's resize handle (180–400, kept while on screen)

rows.feature: Time scale and zoom
rows.what: A fixed week grid (24px a day, week labels); a Day / Week / Month / Quarter zoom exists but is never shown.
rows.v2: Schedule toolbar › Weeks · Months (remembered per browser), with month and week heads
rows.how: Two scales instead of one; Months shows whole quarters.

rows.feature: Today line
rows.what: A red line with a TODAY tag through the grid when today is in range; no scroll to today.
rows.v2: Schedule › today's line, and the toolbar's Today
rows.how: The timeline opens with today about a third of the way in, and Today scrolls back to it.

rows.feature: Calendar days, inclusive
rows.what: All dates are calendar days, a bar's length counts both ends; no weekends, holidays or working days.
rows.v2: Schedule › calendar days, both ends counted, weekends shaded
rows.how: Weekends are shaded; still no holiday calendar.

rows.feature: How state is drawn on bars and rows
rows.what: Bars wear the milestone's own colour; completed = half opacity, at risk = red gradient and pulse, in progress = pulsing row border; blocked has no style.
rows.v2: Schedule › bars by status (done green, running primary filled with its tasks done, blocked red edge, waiting amber stripes, late red edge), a status icon and a line of words per row
rows.how: Status is never colour alone: the row's line says it (“Blocked · waiting on the plumber · was due Fri 18 Sep, 18 days late”).

rows.feature: A bar's own colour
rows.what: Eight swatches in the drawer (Purple, Green, Amber, Red, Blue, Violet, Gold, Slate) set the bar's colour.
rows.v2: Milestone panel › When › Bar colour (By status, or one of eight)
rows.how: Optional: a bar is coloured by its status unless a colour is picked.

rows.feature: At risk
rows.what: A milestone not done whose end passed or with under 20% of its time left is at risk: red bar, a badge, the On Track figure.
rows.v2: Schedule › a milestone past its last day reads overdue / “n days late” in red; the bell warns the alerts lead time before it ends
rows.how: No “under 20% left” rule: late means not done and past its end; the early warning is a reminder.

rows.feature: Critical path
rows.what: Milestones with no float get a red left border on their name row (not on bars).
rows.v2: Schedule › a cap at the end of the bar that decides the handover; its panel says “This one decides the handover date.”
rows.how: Only the one milestone the handover hangs on today, through its links — not a whole critical path.

rows.feature: Payment and commission pills on the chart
rows.what: A yellow chip “S$6,000 · 10%” in the name list and tiny payment and commission pills under a payment milestone's bar.
rows.v2: Schedule › a payment diamond on the bar and a “30% · 21 Aug” chip on the row
rows.how: Shows the tied stage's share and due day; no commission figure.

rows.feature: Dependency arrows
rows.what: Curves from a predecessor's end to a successor's start, red and dashed when broken; one click on an arrow deletes the link with no confirm.
rows.v2: Schedule › link lines between bars (red dashed when broken, lit while a move carries them)
rows.how: Drawn but not clickable; a link is changed in the milestone's panel.

rows.feature: Row controls: eye, bin, variance alert
rows.what: Each name row carries an eye (visible to client), a bin on hover (delete), at-risk / blocked icons and a red alert when an invoice differs.
rows.v2: Schedule › each row: grip, status icon, name, its line, a chip; Mark done and ⋮ at the end
rows.how: Showing to the client is a switch in the panel; Delete is in ⋮ with Undo; an invoice's difference lives on Money.

rows.feature: Milestones without dates
rows.what: Undated milestones get consecutive 7-day slots on load; the drawer shows “Dates not set” and a Set dates mode.
rows.v2: Every milestone has real dates, start on or before end, checked on the server
rows.how: Nothing is undated, so there is no set-dates mode.

rows.feature: Drag a bar to move it
rows.what: The bar follows the pointer and snaps to whole days on release; no date shown while dragging, no Escape, no undo; works with touch.
rows.v2: Schedule › drag a bar
rows.how: Dates show while it moves, Escape puts it back, the timeline scrolls at its edge, it answers in one sentence with Undo; on touch a long press lifts it; on a phone dates move in the panel.

rows.feature: Drag a bar's end to change its length
rows.what: Only the right edge can be dragged; an end before the start is discarded.
rows.v2: Schedule › drag either end of a bar
rows.how: Both ends can be dragged.

rows.feature: Cascade preview before a move applies
rows.what: When dependents must shift, a Dependency Cascade dialog lists them (old → new start, project end change); Cancel throws the whole move away; it pushes only forward and only for drags.
rows.v2: Schedule › followers light up during the move and move with it; the sentence names how many followed; Undo puts all back
rows.how: No dialog first; followers keep their gap either way (earlier too), and typed dates carry them as drags do.

rows.feature: Reorder milestones
rows.what: Drag a name row (native drag-and-drop, not on touch) to a new place; order is renumbered.
rows.v2: Schedule › drag a row by its grip; row ⋮ › Move up / Move down (Alt ↑ ↓)
rows.how: Works on touch, Escape cancels, and it answers with its new place and Undo.

rows.feature: Pick what a milestone depends on
rows.what: Adjust Dependencies lists earlier milestones to tick as predecessors (finish-to-start, all must finish), refuses a loop; no lag days.
rows.v2: Milestone panel › When › Moves with, and It also waits for
rows.how: Several predecessors kept; each link keeps a gap in days (negative = overlap), which 1.0 never shipped; loops refused on the server; links are followed on every move.

rows.feature: The milestone drawer
rows.what: Selecting a row or bar opens a right drawer with name, a summary row (status, dates, colour), description and a list of ten actions each opening its own dialog; the backdrop and Escape do nothing.
rows.v2: Milestone panel (a side panel 560 wide; a bottom sheet on a phone)
rows.how: Fields edit in the panel itself (status, When, links, tasks, invoices, switches) with one Save; Escape or × closes it and asks before dropping edits.

rows.feature: Rename a milestone
rows.what: Double-click the name for an inline box, or type in the drawer's name field (saved on every keystroke).
rows.v1: Gantt › name row; drawer name field
rows.v2: Row ⋮ › Rename (a dialog); on a phone the panel's Name field
rows.how: Saved once, with the sentence.

rows.feature: A milestone's description
rows.what: A short text under the summary, saved on blur or ⌘↵.
rows.v2: Milestone panel › Description

rows.feature: Delete a milestone
rows.what: The bin asks “Delete Milestone… cannot be undone”; links pointing at it are left dangling and nothing stops deleting a published or invoiced one.
rows.v2: Row ⋮ › Delete, or the panel's Delete milestone (asks, then Undo)
rows.how: What followed it is relinked to what it followed, its tasks stay, its payment is untied, and Undo brings all of it back.

rows.feature: Start a milestone
rows.what: “Start this milestone?” then “Started — what next?” offering Post an update or Create tasks; starting demotes any other running milestone; the actual start is promised but not logged.
rows.v2: Status › In progress, then a band “{m} has started — tell {client}, or line up its tasks” with Post an update · Add tasks
rows.how: No confirm step; several milestones may run at once; the day it really started is logged (“Started Mon 5 Oct, 2 days late”).

rows.feature: Post an update from a milestone
rows.what: Post Update in the drawer shares progress on the homeowner's feed with the milestone as context.
rows.v2: The started / done band's Post an update (the Updates composer, the milestone picked); Mark done sheet › Add photos
rows.how: Offered at a start and a Done rather than always in the panel; the Updates composer can pick any milestone.

rows.feature: A milestone's tasks
rows.what: View / Edit Tasks: a list with done / overdue counts; add by Enter; per task assign (members, the homeowner, an outside person, + Add person), due date, description, pictures; batch Save tasks.
rows.v2: Milestone panel › Tasks: tick, add by name (due on its last day, the team on it), open one in place — due date and time, members, description, outside person with Send on WhatsApp, Open in Tasks
rows.how: Each change saves at once; pictures are added in the Tasks tab; a task cannot go to the client, and an outside person is not invited into the studio.

rows.feature: AI task suggestions for a milestone
rows.what: Suggest from quote asks the AI for five to eight tasks for the milestone's phase (and silently returns canned tasks when the AI fails).
rows.v1: View / Edit Tasks › Suggest from quote
rows.how: AI-written task lists wait (no metered press in Projects).

rows.feature: Mark a milestone blocked
rows.what: A dialog (reason: vendor, client, permit, other; details; expected resume date) sets Blocked; a separate popover on the name stores a block without changing the status.
rows.v1: Milestone drawer › Mark as Blocked; name popover
rows.v2: Milestone panel › Status › Blocked; Waiting on someone (the client, a member, a supplier · what for · until); What {client} reads
rows.how: No reason categories (a permit is said in What for); a wait can be set without blocking; the client reads “Paused” with the words the studio chose.

rows.feature: Reschedule a milestone
rows.what: New start and end with an optional reason (stored as a comment nobody sees), then “Publish to homeowner?” — Save without publishing or Publish now (which skips the payment gate).
rows.v2: Milestone panel › When (Starts · Ends, Push it later by 1 day · 3 days · 1 week)
rows.how: No reason field and no publish step — changes wait for Share changes; a new date carries what follows.

rows.feature: Edit a milestone's payment structure
rows.what: Payment % of contract (≈ S$), a commission switch, a live totals strip; frozen after the quote unless an owner presses Override (logged on the lead); locked once invoiced.
rows.how: A milestone ties to a stage of the quote's payment schedule instead (A payment falls due here).

rows.feature: Ask mAIson about a milestone
rows.what: Opens the assistant with “Help me with the {milestone} milestone… what should I be paying attention to?”.
rows.v2: Maison AI on the Schedule tab: What is overdue on this project? · Draft a schedule from the quote · Tell {client} about the new dates
rows.how: Suggestions are for the whole schedule; nothing asks about one milestone.

rows.feature: A milestone's invoices (Related files)
rows.what: Lists the milestone's invoices with number, status and amount, each opening a quick view.
rows.v2: Milestone panel › Invoices (each opens on Money)

rows.feature: A milestone's publish history
rows.what: The last three publishes with what changed (Renamed, Dates shifted by +3d, Status …).
rows.v2: Milestone panel › the last three shares under Shown to {client}

rows.feature: Publish one milestone from its drawer
rows.what: “Unpublished changes — homeowner sees the previous state” with Publish, which publishes this milestone at once.
rows.v2: Milestone panel › “Not shared with {client} yet” and Share this change
rows.how: Opens Share changes with that one change ticked, so the client's preview is seen first.

rows.feature: Invoice variance on a milestone
rows.what: A red banner in the drawer when an invoice was billed over or under the expected amount, with Know more & fix.
rows.v2: Project › Money (an invoice that differs says so and needs a reason)
rows.how: The schedule no longer carries invoice differences.

rows.feature: Milestone statuses
rows.what: Five: not started, in progress, completed, pending approval, blocked; at risk and overdue worked out; finalized is a separate stamp.
rows.v2: Four: Not started · In progress · Blocked · Done (Done stamps its day); a Done waiting for approval is a flag, not a status
rows.how: No pending-approval status and no finalized stamp.

rows.feature: Changing status
rows.what: The status pill offers only allowed moves (Start, Mark complete, Mark as blocked, Reset, Unblock, Reopen with an invoice warning, Withdraw approval request).
rows.v2: Milestone panel › Status (four segments); row ⋮ › the four statuses
rows.how: Any status from any; Done opens the Mark done sheet; every other change answers in one sentence with Undo.

rows.feature: Only one milestone in progress at a time
rows.what: Starting a milestone puts every other running one back to Not started, with a toast.
rows.how: Several milestones may run at once — phases overlap on site.

rows.feature: An owner approves a non-owner's completion
rows.what: With Workflow › Milestone approval required on, a non-owner's Mark as Complete sets Pending approval instead (no task or notice is raised); extra approvers can be added.
rows.v1: Accounts › Workflow Rules › Milestone approval required; Complete Milestone dialog
rows.v2: Settings › Projects › What waits for an Owner or an Admin › Milestone completion needs approval (off by default); the panel's Approve as done / Send back; Overview › Needs your OK
rows.how: Owners and Admins approve (no extra approvers list); the ask is on the record and their bell, and the Done's ticks run on approval.

rows.feature: Project progress %
rows.what: Payment-weighted: completed milestones count their payment %, running ones half; equal weights when no %; the portal can show a different number.
rows.v1: Project page ring, financial card, portal
rows.v2: Progress = milestones done of all (Overview › Progress, the projects list's Progress, the portal)
rows.how: Not weighted by payment share and no half credit for a running one.

rows.feature: Mark a milestone complete
rows.what: A three-step dialog: confirm (with an editable invoice preview) → invoice & link (send or request approval) → post an update “Milestone completed: {name}”.
rows.v1: Milestone drawer › Mark as Complete; status › Mark complete
rows.v2: Mark {stage} done sheet (row's Mark done, ⋮, panel Status › Done, a phone row's Done, an Overview row)
rows.how: One sheet: the day it ended, bring what follows forward, show it on the client's schedule and ask them to confirm, add photos, send the stage's invoice — each tick optional, one Undo.

rows.feature: Completing a payment milestone creates its invoice
rows.what: Confirming creates a draft invoice for contract × %, refused in Draft or when one exists, skipped with no contract value.
rows.v2: Invoices are drafted with the project; a Done makes its stage's invoice Ready to send; the Mark done sheet's Send the {stage} invoice
rows.how: No invoice is made at completion; the milestone only moves the existing draft to Ready (money rules belong to Money).

rows.feature: The homeowner hears a milestone is complete
rows.what: Completing sends the homeowner a bell “Milestone complete: {name}” (desktop: payment milestones only; phone: every one).
rows.v1: Complete Milestone dialog / phone Mark Done
rows.v2: The client's bell and email when the Done is shown on their schedule; “Confirm that … is done” when asked to confirm
rows.how: Nothing reaches the client until the Done is shared; the email goes through the delivery layer developers wire to a provider.

rows.feature: Completion checklist and Finalize
rows.what: A completed milestone shows a checklist (homeowner approval, invoice shared, internal approval) and Finalize Completion locks it once all pass.
rows.v1: Milestone drawer › Completion checklist · Finalize Completion
rows.how: The client confirms only when asked and is never a gate; a Done makes its invoice Ready; invoice approval is Money's.

rows.feature: Answer a revision request with what changed
rows.what: Mark resolved asks what changed, clears the homeowner's response and stores the note as a comment nobody sees.
rows.v2: Milestone panel › the client's answer › Mark resolved (a note the client reads) · Ask {client} again
rows.how: The note shows under that stage on the client's schedule; asking again is a tick, on by default.

rows.feature: Homeowner response banner
rows.what: Above the sub-tabs a red banner lists revision requests and a green strip says a milestone was approved (dismissed per browser); its rows open nothing.
rows.v2: Overview › Needs you (a stage the client says is not right), the row's line on the Schedule, the bell, Needs attention
rows.how: Each answer opens its milestone; confirmations show on the row's line instead of a banner.

rows.feature: The homeowner approves a milestone or asks for a revision
rows.what: The portal's “Milestones to Confirm” lists published milestones shown as completed or pending approval: Approve, or Request Revision with a note; one answer each.
rows.v2: Portal › Schedule: Looks good · Something is not right, on a stage the studio asked about
rows.how: Only for a stage shared as done that the studio asked about; never a gate; the answer stays on its row and the studio can ask again.

rows.feature: The studio hears the client's answer
rows.what: milestone.homeowner_approved and milestone.homeowner_revision_requested reach owners, admins and the team (a revision also by WhatsApp template).
rows.v2: Bell events A client confirms a finished stage · A client says something is not right with a stage (Settings › Notifications)

rows.feature: The client sees a published copy, not live edits
rows.what: Publishing copies name, dates and status per milestone; status changes publish themselves; block details and payment % reach the homeowner live without a publish.
rows.v2: Share changes stores a copy the portal reads — never live rows
rows.how: A status change waits for a share too; only a pause leaks live, and only in the words the studio wrote for the client.

rows.feature: First-publish wizard
rows.what: Four steps before the first publish: tag payment %, confirm the quote's scope, check the total is 100%, review; also reopened from Reconfigure homeowner view and Rebalance.
rows.how: The first share sends the whole schedule with a preview; payments come from the quote.

rows.feature: Publish several changes at once
rows.what: Publish to homeowner lists milestones with changes (Name / Start / End / Status old → new, First publish), each ticked, with Select all.
rows.v2: Share changes dialog: what changes for {client} (struck → new), a tick per change, a note, and What {client} will see

rows.feature: What a publish records
rows.what: Stamps each milestone's publish time and copy and appends a history entry (kept to 20).
rows.v2: Each share stores its copy, its changes, the note, who and when, and an Activity line

rows.feature: “Schedule updated” update posted to the homeowner
rows.what: When a published milestone's dates change, publishing posts a homeowner progress update “Schedule updated: {name}” with old and new dates.
rows.v2: The share's note and “Updated {day} · Handover is now …” on the client's schedule; the portal marks what moved since they last looked
rows.how: No automatic progress update.

rows.feature: The client is told the timeline was published
rows.what: project.timeline_published emails the first linked homeowner (“Your timeline has been updated”, Open portal) when the studio allows it.
rows.v2: Client's bell and email “Your schedule is ready / has changed”; Tell {client} on WhatsApp offered after the share
rows.how: The email goes through the delivery layer (a stand-in developers wire to a provider); WhatsApp opens a drafted message on the press.

rows.feature: The studio team is told of a publish
rows.what: The same event puts “Timeline Published to Homeowner” on the studio roles' bell and email.
rows.v2: Activity › “{who} shared n changes to the schedule with the client”
rows.how: No bell or email to the team; only the Activity line (and whoever asked to share hears it).

rows.feature: Which milestones the client sees
rows.what: An eye per row (hidden by default for non-payment milestones) while publishing treats anything not hidden as visible; the eye takes effect at once; there is no unpublish.
rows.v2: Milestone panel › Shown to {client} (one switch, on by default)
rows.how: One meaning; switching it off takes the stage off the client's copy at the next share (“Taken off the schedule”).

rows.feature: Changes need approval before the client sees them
rows.what: Workflow › Timeline approval required is shown but has no effect since the timeline approval flow was removed.
rows.v1: Accounts › Workflow Rules › Timeline approval required
rows.v2: Settings › Projects › What waits for an Owner or an Admin › Schedule changes need approval before the client sees them (off by default)
rows.how: It works: a Designer's or a Manager's Share asks an Owner or an Admin, who shares it or sends it back with a note.

rows.feature: What the homeowner's timeline shows
rows.what: A Timeline card: filter chips (All, Payments, In progress, Blocked, Upcoming), milestones with payment pills and Paid, a paused box with “Resuming around …”, sent invoices and Project Created on the rail, one Active row.
rows.v2: Portal › Schedule: stages with dates and state, the payments under each stage, Paused with the studio's words, the “you are here” row, what changed
rows.how: No filter chips, no invoice or Project Created events on the rail, and a paused stage gives no resume day (a project on hold does).

rows.feature: Payment milestones
rows.what: A milestone with a payment % (or a fixed amount) is a payment milestone; together they are the project's billing schedule.
rows.v2: Milestone panel › A payment falls due here (a stage of the quote's payment schedule; when it starts or when it is done)
rows.how: The share comes from the quote's schedule (or a direct project's split) and never moves; the milestone only says when it falls due, one stage per milestone.

rows.feature: Payment and commission overview under the chart
rows.what: Under the chart: a commission-not-set strip, VO chips, four tiles (contract, expected and received payments, commission, progress) and a ledger of payment milestones and their status.
rows.v2: Project › Money (Billing: stages, invoices, what is paid); Schedule summary › Next payment
rows.how: Money's one set of numbers; the schedule keeps only the next payment and the diamonds.

rows.feature: A frozen payment schedule and its override
rows.what: Once any milestone has a %, the schedule is frozen; a user with the payment-schedule override permission unlocks it (logged on the lead).
rows.how: Agreed shares never move on the schedule.

rows.feature: Timeline payments copied into the quote
rows.what: Every timeline save mirrors payment milestones into the lead's contract quote's payment schedule.
rows.how: The quote's payment schedule is the source; nothing flows back from the schedule.

rows.feature: Commission triggered by a milestone
rows.what: A milestone can be flagged to trigger commission (accruing on completion or finalize), shown as a “Comm: S$…” pill.
rows.v1: New milestone / Payment Structure › Trigger commission
rows.v2: Company › Finance › Commission; Settings › Finance › Commission
rows.how: Commission is earned on the client's payments (or the profit, or a fixed amount), never on a milestone.

rows.feature: Complete a milestone from the invoice flow
rows.what: Create Invoice lists the payment milestones; an unfinished one offers “Complete & Invoice…”, which marks it completed (or pending approval) before the invoice is composed.
rows.v1: Project › Finance › Create Invoice; a timeline chip's Complete & bill…
rows.v2: Money › Billing names the milestone a stage's draft waits on (“Sent when Carpentry is done”); the Mark done sheet marks it done and sends that invoice in one press
rows.how: Completion happens on the Schedule (or from an Overview row), not inside the invoice flow; the invoice was drafted with the project.

rows.feature: A variation order's extra days on the timeline
rows.what: A VO carries timeline impact days; the Gantt's VO chip sums the approved ones (“+S$1,200 (+3d)”) and the VO paper and the portal print them; nothing moves the milestones.

rows.feature: At-risk milestone task for the owner
rows.what: While an owner has the page open, each at-risk milestone raises a task “At-risk milestone: {name}” due today.
rows.v2: Bell “Overdue: {milestone}” for the project's team; Needs attention “n milestones overdue”; Overview › Needs you
rows.how: Raised on the server for every project, as bell rows rather than tasks, and not only when someone opens the page.

rows.feature: Upcoming-milestone review task (Proactive Alerts)
rows.what: With Proactive Alerts on, each milestone due within the lead time (default 7 days) raises a review task for the owner.
rows.v2: Bell “Ends in n days: {milestone}”; Settings › Projects › Schedule › Alerts lead time (1–30, 3 by default)
rows.how: A bell row for the team instead of an owner's task; switched off per event in Settings › Notifications.

rows.feature: Extension request settings
rows.what: Proactive Alerts › Notify owner on extension request and Auto-create progress update — but the extension request itself has no screen.
rows.v1: Accounts › Proactive Alerts › Extension Request Settings
rows.v2: Milestone panel › Ask for more time (Designers and Managers); Owners and Admins Approve / Decline, with “Draft an update for {client} with the new day”
rows.how: The ask works and always reaches Owners and Admins' bell; the update is a draft ticked on approval, not posted at the ask.

rows.feature: The schedule as a card list
rows.what: Below 1024px: a card per milestone with status icon, payment %, date line (“· 5d overdue”), task count, a re-date button and a blocked strip; it reads old in-milestone tasks the desk no longer writes.
rows.v2: Schedule on a phone: rows with a thin bar to scale and today's line, the row's line and payment share, the panel as a bottom sheet
rows.how: The same milestones and tasks as the desk.

rows.feature: Mark Done on a phone
rows.what: Mark Done completes at once (skipping Start and the completion dialog); on a payment milestone it asks “Complete & invoice”, then gives no link to the invoice.
rows.v2: A phone row's Done, or the project's site bar Done → the Mark done sheet
rows.how: The same sheet as the desk: the client and the invoice follow its ticks.

rows.feature: Add and re-date on a phone
rows.what: Add milestone opens the desk's dialog; the re-date button opens Reschedule, whose Publish now does nothing on a phone.
rows.v2: Add milestone at the foot; dates in the panel's When
rows.how: No publish step; Share N changes sits beside the who-sees line.

rows.feature: What a phone cannot do
rows.what: A phone cannot start, block, link, pay, hide, rename, colour, delete, reorder, publish, see approvals or finalize.
rows.v2: On a phone everything the desk does except dragging bars (the panel's ⋮ Move up · Move down · Add a milestone after)
rows.how: Dates move in the panel instead of by drag.

rows.feature: Read-only after closing, and the handover lock
rows.what: A Closed project hides the drawer's actions; with the lock-on-handover feature a locked project disables edits unless the user may override.
rows.v2: A completed project's schedule reads only, refused on the server; the panel says why; Reopen opens it again
rows.how: One rule on the server instead of a lock feature and an override permission; the panel still shows a milestone's dates, status and tasks.

rows.feature: Who may change a timeline
rows.what: Any signed-in studio member; every rule is in the browser and the whole array is written as sent, last write wins.
rows.v2: The project's team, Owners and Admins change the schedule; Who sees leads decides who sees it; every rule is checked on the server
rows.how: Rules live on the server; Settings › Who may do what lists them.

rows.feature: Close the project from the Milestones pane
rows.what: A “Wrap up this project” card with Close Project sits under the Milestones pane of an Active project.
rows.v2: Overview › Needs you / the header's Complete handover
rows.how: Handing over is the stage's own action, not a card on the schedule.

rows.feature: Tasks tied to a milestone
rows.what: Tasks saved from a milestone carry its id, so they also show on the Tasks sub-tab and /tasks.
rows.v2: Project › Tasks: the Milestone column and filter; a task's Milestone field

rows.feature: mAIson drafts a timeline in chat
rows.what: The assistant's suggest_timeline and generate_project_plan tools return a plan of milestones in the chat (nothing is saved); the home offers “Plan a project timeline”.
rows.v2: Maison AI on the Schedule › Draft a schedule from the quote (opens the draft for review on the Set up card or Rebuild)
rows.how: A scripted suggestion that opens the curated draft; there is no chat agent.

new_in_2.feature: Ask for more time on a milestone
new_in_2.v2: Milestone panel › Ask for more time; a Designer's drag past a running milestone's end opens the ask
new_in_2.note: Owners and Admins approve (the dates move, with what follows) or decline with a note; 1.0's extension request was code with no screen.

new_in_2.v2: Schedule › a focused bar: ← → a day, Shift a week, Alt its end; J / K walk rows; the ? panel lists them
new_in_2.note: 1.0's Gantt had no keyboard at all.

new_in_2.v2: Schedule › a dashed outline where the client last saw a bar, a “+1 week” chip, “later than first shared” in the panel
Milestone panel › Waiting on someone (the client, a member, a supplier)
new_in_2.note: The project then reads waiting; sharing a choice starts the wait and a pick ends it.

new_in_2.v2: Mark done sheet › Done on, Bring {next} forward
new_in_2.note: A milestone done before its last day ends that day; what follows may come forward.

new_in_2.v2: Every move, status, save, delete, rebuild, share answer
new_in_2.note: One sentence and Undo; the Activity line goes with it.
Every add, rename, move, status, delete, share and ask has its line.

new_in_2.v2: Projects list › Next milestone and Progress columns; Needs attention; Reports › Projects overdue milestones

new_in_2.note: Mark done, Start, Share, approvals and the client's concerns, each with its one button.

new_in_2.feature: The schedule in Start the project
new_in_2.v2: Project header › Start the project sheet › The schedule
new_in_2.note: Start, schedule, invite and deposit in one press.

new_in_2.feature: What changed since the client last looked
new_in_2.note: Moved and new stages are marked on the client's own page.

new_in_2.feature: The site bar on a phone
new_in_2.v2: Project page on a phone while In progress › Photos · Done · Note · Message
new_in_2.note: A milestone done in two presses on site.

notes: Nothing was run in either app; every 1.0 row is from inventory E (and B's and J's schedule rows) spot-checked in the 1.0 code, and every 2.0 counterpart was opened in the working tree. 1.0 code that has no screen was left out as rows: milestone comments, the extension-request handler, zoom controls, link-by-drag, lag-day arrows, Generate tasks, the Draft wizard's schedule step, Clone (which copies the timeline), the offline mark_milestone queue and the TimelineApproval task links. One gap no inventory listed as its own row: a variation order's timeline impact days (the “+3d” on 1.0's VO chip), which nothing in 2.0 carries. Every schedule email and WhatsApp to the client or the team rides 2.0's delivery layer, a stand-in until developers wire a provider. The portal's own schedule page and the money behind payment stages are mapped here only where they meet the schedule; their readers own the detail.
